**Description**
At Audible, we believe stories have the power to transform lives. It’s why we work with some of the world’s leading creators to produce and share audio storytelling with our millions of global listeners. We are dreamers and inventors who come from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences to empower and inspire each other. Imagine your future with us.
  
  
**About This Role**
As a Software Development Engineer, it’s up to you to define, design and refine the tech that keeps us one step ahead of listeners. Anticipate. Innovate. Bring challenging ideas and we’ll support you with the latest tech, tools, and systems that you need to succeed. We pride ourselves on our ability to imagine and invent solutions to problems of the future. You’ll be essential in this forward-thinking approach to development. Together with the team, you’ll build and maintain our platform to bring thousands of stories to millions of listeners and unleash the power of the human voice.
  
  
**About You**
If you’re a dedicated problem solver, this is the role for you. Identifying and overcoming challenges is at the heart of everything you do; whether it’s looking ahead to our listeners problems, or analyzing every inefficiency, you thrive when you strive for perfection. We look for people who take responsibility, who feel the pride in a job well done and see every failure as an opportunity to learn. With a knowledgeable team around you, and opportunities to challenge yourself, it’s a perfect environment to develop and apply your new skills.
  
  
As a Software Development Engineer, you will...
  
  

* Develop, test, and maintain software components and applications for the world's largest audiobook creator and provider
* Identify and resolve software defects through code review, log analysis, metrics examination, debugging, and other troubleshooting methods
* Write maintainable and scalable code for software components as part of an agile engineering team
* Collaborate with stakeholders to envision, design, develop, test, and launch customer-centric software that inspires and impacts users
* Apply computer science, engineering, and analysis principles to solve moderate-scale problems
* Continuously enhance testability, operational excellence (OE), and documentation for owned software components
* Handle data classification, storage, and management in accordance with company policies
* Participate in the interview process and provide mentorship to fellow engineers

**About Audible**
Audible is the leading producer and provider of audio storytelling. We spark listeners’ imaginations, offering immersive, cinematic experiences full of inspiration and insight to enrich our customers daily lives. We are a global company with an entrepreneurial spirit. We are dreamers and inventors who are passionate about the positive impact Audible can make for our customers and our neighbors. This spirit courses throughout Audible, supporting a culture of creativity and inclusion built on our People Principles and our mission to build more equitable communities in the cities we call home.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

**Description**
We are seeking Applied Scientists to join Amazon. In this role, you will develop and deploy the science of safe autonomy on highly dynamic robots, advancing the frontier through both foundational research and realization on hardware. You will contribute to achieving safe autonomy across three key areas: control barrier function (CBF) theory for robust and performant safety on hardware; safe reinforcement learning for agile whole-body control; and layered safety filters that interface with learning, perception, and semantic reasoning systems. You will validate your work experimentally on state-of-the-art robotic platforms — removing bottlenecks to deployment and enabling robots to safely operate around humans. You will work with the inventor of CBFs, as well as top scientists and engineers at Amazon developing the next generation of safe autonomy.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Advance the science of safe autonomy from formal foundations to the integration with learning and perception to validation on hardware — with particular emphasis on methods that bridge these domains.
* Test and validate hardware, with a focus on next generation robotic systems. Including locomotion, manipulation and loco-manipulation.
* Leverage the deployments on hardware to validate the underlying science, identifying gaps between theory and practice that drive the next cycle of research. hardware to validate the underlying science, identifying gaps between theory and practice that drive the next cycle of research.
* Publish research at top-tier robotics, control, and ML venues, and contribute to Amazon’s scientific reputation in advanced robotics.
* Collaborate with SAF Lab and Amazon production teams to move research into robots deployed at Amazon scale.

**About The Team**
The Safe Autonomy Frontiers (SAF) Lab is the first industry research lab dedicated to safe autonomy, founded by the inventor of control barrier functions. We are developing a universal safety layer for the next generation of robotic systems: mobile robots, manipulators, quadrupeds, and humanoids. Here you will advance performant safety for highly dynamic robots — CBF theory integrated with perception and learning, evaluated on next-generation platforms — and your work will underpin robots operating alongside people at Amazon’s unprecedented scale.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* PhD or equivalent research experience
* Master’s degree and 3+ years of applied science, research, or robotics engineering experience — OR a PhD — in computer science, robotics, control, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field.
* Hands-on experience developing and deploying control algorithms and/or learning policies on physical robotic hardware in a research or production setting (not simulation-only).
* Working knowledge of safety-critical control, including control barrier functions and safety filters.
* Proficiency in C++ and Python, with a track record of implementing control algorithms and/or learning policies in real systems.
* Experience with physics simulators for robotics (e.g., Isaac Gym/Sim, MuJoCo, PyBullet).
* Demonstrated technical impact through shipped systems, patents, or publications at top-tier venues (e.g., CDC, ACC, L-CSS, ICRA, IROS, RSS, RA-L, Automatica, TAC, TRO).

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in professional software development, including production code quality, testing, and deployment practices.
* Experience taking robotics or autonomy research from prototype to deployed product, including collaboration with hardware, product, and operations teams.
* Understanding of autonomous systems, reduced-order models, layered control architectures, nonlinear control, reachability methods, legged locomotion, and whole-body control.
* Knowledge of learning-based approaches to robotics (e.g., reinforcement learning, diffusion, VLAs, VLMs, world models).
* Exposure learning-based approaches for CBF synthesis (e.g., neural CBFs, data-driven barrier functions) and the integration of CBFs into learning (e.g., CBF-RL).
* Understanding of control systems engineering, with a focus on layered architecture in robotic systems (high-level planning, mid-level trajectory generation, low-level feedback control).
* Experience with perception on robotic systems (e.g., depth-camera and LiDAR-based sensing, sensor fusion, semantic tagging), together with mapping and navigation.
* Familiarity with Hamilton-Jacobi reachability analysis and its relationship to CBF-based approaches.
* Knowledge of safety-constrained RL (e.g., constrained MDPs, Lagrangian methods, shielding, CBF-based policy filtering).
* Experience with model-based control (MPC, whole-body QP controllers, operational space control) and/or simulation-based predictive control (MPPI).
* Experience with hierarchical RL, skill composition, distillation, and multi-task policy architectures for locomotion.
* Familiarity with real-time deployment constraints (latency budgets, onboard compute limitations, control-loop frequencies).
* Experience building or contributing to large-scale RL training infrastructure (distributed training, GPU clusters).
* Strong communication skills and ability to work across disciplinary boundaries (ML, controls, mechanical engineering).

Job Description
  
  
The Data Analyst I is responsible for implementing best information technology data management practices in an effort to improve and ensure quality, streamline data cleaning efforts and deliver analyzable databases within agreed upon project timelines.
  
  
The Data Analyst I will primarily support the quantitative component of AIM-UP, a research project examining how evidence-based adolescent pregnancy prevention programs are adapted for diverse populations and settings. Drawing on individual student survey data from nine implementation projects involving more than 17,000 participants across Indiana, the analyst will help manage, integrate, and analyze data to examine how program adaptations relate to participants’ knowledge, attitudes, skills, intentions, and behaviors. The analyst will also work as part of a statistical core supporting the Department of Surgery, assisting with research data management, development of analysis plans, statistical analyses, and preparation of tables, figures, and methods and results sections for manuscripts. Additional projects may involve similar data management and analytical responsibilities, with work conducted in collaboration with investigators and under statistical guidance.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Designs and writes custom applications needed to ensure the database meets requirements for the entry, management and reporting of data.
* Assists in the development of data management plans and guidelines that will deliver accurate, timelines consistent with quality data. Assures the quality control compliance process.
* Identifies and implements solutions to data management issues and concerns that arise during the conduct of research studies.
* Assists staff with technical issues related to electronic and remote record keeping systems; trains staff to help improve quality of data collected.
* Assists medical students, interns, residents and/or program faculty with queries and generating statistical analyses.
* Maintains knowledge of the current regulations and technologies related to data management.
* May write and prepare manuscripts and other materials for internal and external audiences.
* Uses R to clean, merge, and efficiently process large, complex research datasets; uses SQL to query and retrieve data as needed.
* Develops automated data quality reports, tables, and figures using R Markdown or Quarto.
* Uses the REDCap API to automate data imports and exports, as appropriate.
* Uses Git or other version control tools to maintain documented code and support collaborative programming.
* Prepares and supports analyses of longitudinal and clustered research data, including repeated measurements and data collected across schools or study sites.
* Performs other related duties.

**About The Company**
DataAnnotation works with advanced artificial intelligence systems, helping improve how they understand and respond to complex questions. The company brings subject-matter experts into the development process so that AI models can be evaluated against accurate, carefully reasoned examples. In chemistry, this work is especially important: a response may sound convincing while proposing an impossible mechanism, an unsafe condition, or a result that does not align with physical principles. DataAnnotation is building a growing area of work focused on teaching models to reason correctly, not simply produce plausible-sounding answers.
  
  
**About The Role**
DataAnnotation is seeking an experienced Computational Chemist – AI Trainer to create, test, and validate challenging chemistry tasks for leading AI models. You will use your research expertise and coding skills to identify gaps in a model’s chemical reasoning and develop problems that reliably expose them. Each task you submit must include a defensible answer and a clear standard for evaluating model performance. Your task and solution will serve as ground truth, so accuracy, reproducibility, and scientific rigor are essential.
  
  
This is an independent contractor opportunity with flexible project selection and scheduling. Work remotely using your own computer, and take on projects that match your expertise and availability. Applicants must be located in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, or the United States.
  
  
**Qualifications**
You are an active researcher or experienced practitioner in chemistry or chemical engineering, such as an advanced graduate student, postdoctoral researcher, academic researcher, or industry professional. You bring deep knowledge in one or more relevant areas, including computational or physical chemistry, cheminformatics, molecular modeling, or analytical workflows. You are fluent in English at a native or bilingual level and can explain technical reasoning clearly in writing.
  
  
Strong coding skills are required. You write Python and are comfortable working at a terminal as a regular part of your research, including using code to investigate, solve, or validate scientific problems. Familiarity with reproducible workflows or containerized environments, such as Docker, is an advantage. You should be able to assess whether a proposed answer is chemically valid and support your conclusions with a transparent, reproducible rationale.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Design complex, original chemistry tasks within your areas of expertise. Define the expected correct answer and the criteria a model must meet, then independently test and validate each task before submitting it. Provide a step-by-step solution that another researcher can follow and reproduce.
  
  
Create tasks that require genuine chemical reasoning rather than recall or replay of a familiar answer. Evaluate model responses and identify where reasoning fails, including impossible mechanisms, unsafe conditions, unphysical results, or misinterpreted spectra. Apply appropriate computational tools and scientific judgment to verify findings, and communicate assumptions, methods, and conclusions precisely. Maintain high standards for accuracy and consistency because the submitted work will be used to assess model performance.
  
  
**Benefits**
Choose the projects you want to work on and set your own schedule. Work remotely from your home using your own computer, with flexibility to balance assignments alongside other commitments. Project rates are hourly and may range from $40 to $125 USD per hour, with bonuses available for high-quality work. Payment is made through PayPal, which handles any currency conversion from USD. DataAnnotation will never ask applicants to pay money to participate.
  
  
Equal Opportunity
  
  
DataAnnotation welcomes applicants with relevant expertise and experience from a range of research and professional backgrounds. Selection is based on qualifications, demonstrated skills, and the requirements of the work. Applicants will be considered without discrimination on the basis of legally protected characteristics. This is an independent contractor position, and consideration is limited to applicants located in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

**About Outtake**
Outtake exists to empower and facilitate trust for a digital-first world. Today, impersonation, fraud, AI-driven scams, and identity abuse spread faster than any security team can respond to. So we built something different: an agentic AI platform that proactively detects, monitors, and takes down impersonators, automating protection in hours, not weeks.
  
  
Built by ex-Palantir, ex-CTO/founders, and ex-Notion engineers, Outtake is designed for clarity, autonomy, and velocity. Our goal is ambitious: become the trust layer of the modern internet. And we intend to do it with a lean, dense, exceptionally talented team.

The Role
  
  
This is a platform engineering role. You will own the foundations that product engineers rely on every day, designing and maintaining the systems, tools, and primitives that determine how fast, safely, and confidently the team can ship. Your work directly influences developer workflows, reliability, and day-to-day engineering velocity.
  
  
You will prioritize work that multiplies impact across the engineering org, turning patterns into platforms and one-off fixes into systems rather than solving the same problem repeatedly. The goal is to make it easier for engineers to move quickly and do the right thing by default.
  
  
This is a role that expects you to build durable foundations. You will develop and evolve a point of view on how engineers should work, then translate that vision into code and systems — operating comfortably in messy, fast-moving environments and steadily turning them into something more solid without slowing the team down. You'll balance long-term thinking with practical execution.

* Own the foundations that product engineers rely on every day, including the systems, tools, and primitives that shape developer workflows, reliability, and velocity
* Prioritize work that multiplies impact across the engineering org, turning repeated patterns into platforms and one-off fixes into systems
* Develop and evolve a point of view on how engineers should work, then translate that vision into code and durable systems
* Operate in messy, fast-moving environments and steadily turn them into something more solid without slowing the team down
* Build or own internal platforms, developer tooling, or shared infrastructure that engineers default to
* Remove entire classes of errors through better abstractions rather than one-off fixes
* Build infrastructure that quietly unlocks faster product work across teams
* Become the person other engineers rely on when systems get weird or unclear, and the person leadership turns to when deciding how the platform should evolve next

What We’re Looking For
  
  

* A track record of building and owning foundational systems that other engineers depended on, along with experience living with the consequences of those decisions
* The ability to ramp quickly, operate in ambiguity, and make progress without needing problems fully specified up front
* An understanding of the tension between ideal solutions and velocity, and the judgment to know when to pursue one over the other
* An instinct for leverage, with a preference for systemic fixes over one-off solutions
* A clear point of view on how engineers should work, and the drive to turn that into code, tooling, and defaults
* Experience working closely with other engineers or teams as an enabler, not just as an implementer
* A desire to help define and build the platform's direction, rather than execute against a tightly defined scope and fixed roadmap
* Nice to have: experience building or owning internal platforms, developer tooling, or shared infrastructure
* Nice to have: experience working on agentic systems, LLM platforms, or large-scale data ingestion pipelines
* Nice to have: a track record of being the person people go to when systems get weird or unclear
